subject: biology
title: Catalysis without consumption
stem: A purified enzyme is added to a reaction mixture. The same amount of product is eventually formed with or without the enzyme, but the enzyme-treated mixture reaches this amount sooner. Which conclusion is supported?

verification.method: Original syllabus-linked authoring with explicit mark reconciliation and displayed-data calculations
verification.notes: Guide statements: C1.1.1, C1.1.10.  Original text, constructed data and self-drawn schematic artwork; no licensed question bank adapted.

options.label: A
options.text: The enzyme provides a pathway with lower activation energy.

options.label: B
options.text: The enzyme increases the energy released per reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: The enzyme becomes a permanent part of every product molecule.

options.label: D
options.text: The enzyme supplies all the energy used to break substrate bonds.

steps.text: A. A catalyst lowers activation energy and increases reaction rate. It does not change the overall energy difference between substrates and products or become consumed stoichiometrically.

parts.label: b

steps.text: The substitution can alter interactions stabilizing the overall three-dimensional fold.

title: Immobilized enzyme beads
stem: Lactase is immobilized in porous beads. The beads convert lactose in a stirred solution to products. A student claims that immobilization prevents all enzyme–substrate collisions because the enzyme cannot move freely.

verification.method: Original syllabus-linked authoring with explicit mark reconciliation and displayed-data calculations

title: Two routes to the same products
stem: A constructed energy profile gives the energy of substrates as 20 kJ mol⁻¹ and products as 5 kJ mol⁻¹. The peak is 75 kJ mol⁻¹ without enzyme and 40 kJ mol⁻¹ with enzyme.

verification.method: Original syllabus-linked authoring with explicit mark reconciliation and displayed-data calculations
verification.notes: Guide statements: C1.1.10.  Original text, constructed data and self-drawn schematic artwork; no licensed question bank adapted.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the activation energy for each route.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain whether adding enzyme changes the net energy released by the reaction.

steps.text: Without enzyme: 75−20 = 55 kJ mol⁻¹.
With enzyme: 40−20 = 20 kJ mol⁻¹.
Both routes release 20−5 = 15 kJ mol⁻¹.
The enzyme changes the pathway and its activation barrier, but not the substrate or product energy levels.

subject: biology
title: Saturation at constant enzyme concentration
stem: An assay has excess cofactor, a constant pH and a constant temperature. Increasing substrate concentration from 8 to 16 mmol dm⁻³ causes almost no change in initial rate. Which explanation is most appropriate?

verification.method: Original syllabus-linked authoring with explicit mark reconciliation and displayed-data calculations
verification.notes: Guide statements: C1.1.8.  Original text, constructed data and self-drawn schematic artwork; no licensed question bank adapted.

options.label: A
options.text: The substrate concentration has stopped affecting the number of collisions because molecular motion has ceased.

options.label: B
options.text: Most active sites are occupied for most of the time.

options.label: C
options.text: The enzyme has been consumed by the 8 mmol dm⁻³ substrate.

options.label: D
options.text: Every extra substrate molecule denatures one enzyme molecule.

steps.text: B. At substrate saturation, the available enzyme active sites are already occupied for most of the time, so additional substrate produces little further increase in rate.

title: Where catalysis occurs
stem: Pancreatic protease is secreted into the small intestine. A different enzyme catalyses a step of glycolysis in a pancreatic cell.

steps.text: The protease reaction in the intestinal lumen is extracellular because it occurs outside cells.
The glycolysis reaction is intracellular because it occurs within the cell’s cytoplasm.
Both require specific catalysts that lower activation barriers so biologically useful reaction rates are achieved.

title: Metabolism and body heat

New incoming substrate is required on each turn and is converted to products; regeneration conserves the acceptor, not the incoming substrate.

Increasing substrate cannot displace Y from that site; the attainable rate remains lower.
Other molecular mechanisms can produce similar kinetic patterns; direct binding or structural evidence is needed to locate the site.

title: An altered penicillin target
stem: A constructed experiment compares bacterial transpeptidase before and after exposure to penicillin. The original enzyme remains inactive after free penicillin is removed. A mutant enzyme catalyses cell-wall cross-linking but is much less affected by penicillin.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain how the mutant enzyme can confer resistance without losing all of its normal function.

parts.label: c

steps.text: Penicillin forms a persistent chemical attachment at the active site, causing mechanism-based irreversible inhibition.
Removing unbound inhibitor does not reverse that chemical change to already inhibited enzyme molecules.

stem: A resting neuron has a negative potential inside relative to outside. Its sodium–potassium pumps use ATP to transport sodium out and potassium in, while the membrane is more permeable to potassium than sodium.

steps.text: The pump transports ions against their electrochemical gradients, requiring energy from ATP hydrolysis.

title: Differential elongation in a shoot
stem: In a shoot receiving lateral light, auxin becomes more concentrated on the shaded side. In this shoot, the relevant auxin concentration promotes cell elongation.

parts.label: b

steps.text: Auxin promotes hydrogen-ion secretion into the apoplast/cell-wall space.
Acidification promotes wall loosening, allowing turgor-driven cell expansion and elongation.
Cells on the shaded side elongate more than cells on the illuminated side.
The longer shaded side forces the shoot to curve towards the illuminated side.
Greater length on the illuminated side would bend the shoot away from that side, contrary to the observed response.

subject: biology
title: Coordinating roots and shoots
stem: Root tips and shoot tips exchange plant signals. Cytokinin is produced in root tips, while auxin is produced in shoot tips.

steps.text: Cytokinin is transported from roots towards shoots.
Auxin is transported from shoots towards roots.
Growth of each region can respond to information from the other, helping coordinate root and shoot development rather than allowing fully independent growth.
Responses depend on the balance or interaction of signals, tissue type and conditions, not simply one hormone in isolation.

title: A specific antigen is recognized

Their expansion can produce a faster and larger specific response, reducing the time available for the pathogen to multiply.

title: A test of species association
stem:
Sixty independent randomly placed quadrats give the following constructed presence–absence counts. Use $\chi^2=\sum (O-E)^2/E$. With one degree of freedom, the 5% critical value is 3.84.

||Species B present|Species B absent|
|---|---|---|
|Species A present|22|8|
|Species A absent|8|22|

parts.label: b

title: Food and predation in the Yukon
stem:
In the real Kluane snowshoe-hare experiment, researchers independently manipulated food supply and mammalian predator access. The [1995 research paper](https://boonstraresearch.weebly.com/uploads/1/4/4/1/144120451/krebs.1995.science.impact_of_food_and_predation_on_the_snowshoe_hare_cycle.pdf) reports approximate density multipliers during the population peak and decline, summarized below. These are reported results, not invented counts.

|Treatment|Hare density relative to control|
|---|---|
|Control|1|
|Predator exclusion|2|
|Added food|3|
|Both treatments|11|

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify which manipulation tests top-down control and which tests bottom-up control.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the prediction if the two increases above the control were simply additive, and compare it with the combined result.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain what the combined result suggests about using a single-factor explanation.

parts.label: d

steps.text: Predator exclusion tests top-down control.
Food addition tests bottom-up control.
Control 1 plus the predator-removal increment (2−1) plus the food increment (3−1).
Predicted multiplier = 4; the observed combined multiplier of about 11 is much larger.
Food supply and predation interact, so either factor alone gives an incomplete explanation of hare density under these conditions.
More prey can increase predator survival or reproduction, increasing later predation pressure; fewer prey can have the reverse effect.

title: Contrasting community controls
stem: In a constructed lake study, adding nutrients increases algae and then herbivore biomass. In another lake, reducing fish predators increases herbivores and decreases algae.

steps.text: Nutrient addition illustrates bottom-up control.
Predator reduction illustrates top-down control.
Reduced predation allows more herbivores to survive.
Greater herbivory removes more algae, producing an indirect effect across trophic levels.
Both resources and consumers can affect populations simultaneously, and their relative importance can change with conditions.

subject: biology
title: Chemical suppression of neighbours
stem: Black walnut produces juglone, which can inhibit plant growth in laboratory assays. Penicillium fungi can release penicillin, which inhibits susceptible bacteria. A constructed assay shows reduced seedling growth with purified juglone, while a separate assay shows reduced bacterial growth with penicillin.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain the shared potential benefit to the organism producing the chemical.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the juglone assay alone does not establish that juglone causes all poor growth beneath walnut trees in the field.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: State one piece of additional evidence needed to connect the laboratory effect to a field mechanism.

steps.text: Allelopathy.
An antibiotic.
Suppressing competitors can reduce competition for resources such as space or nutrients.
Laboratory concentration and exposure may differ from field conditions, where shade, roots, water and nutrients also affect growth.
Measure bioavailable juglone at inhibitory concentrations in the relevant field soil, or manipulate juglone independently of shade/root competition and measure plant response.

subject: biology
title: Drawing a system boundary
stem: A stream ecosystem receives sunlight, dissolved nutrients and falling leaves. Water, organisms and heat can leave the study reach. Which system description is appropriate?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

steps.text: B. Internal recycling does not prevent exchanges with the surroundings. The study reach receives and loses both matter and energy, making it an open system.

subject: biology
title: An autotroph without chlorophyll
stem: A bacterium uses energy released when it oxidizes iron compounds to fix carbon dioxide into organic compounds. It does not require light for this process. Which classification is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Photoautotroph.

options.label: B
options.text: Heterotroph, because chemical oxidation rather than light provides its energy.

options.label: C
options.text: Photoautotroph, because carbon dioxide fixation always requires direct absorption of light.

options.label: D
options.text: Chemoautotroph.

steps.text: D. The bacterium obtains carbon from inorganic carbon dioxide and energy from chemical oxidation, so it is a chemoautotroph.

subject: biology
title: Assimilation is not simply ingestion
stem: A herbivore consumes plant protein. Later, some of the plant-derived carbon is found in the herbivore’s muscle proteins and some in carbon dioxide that it releases.

steps.text: Digestion breaks dietary proteins into amino acids.
Absorbed amino acids are used, with appropriate metabolic transformations if needed, to synthesize proteins specified by the herbivore’s cells.
Some carbon compounds are oxidized in respiration and their carbon is released as carbon dioxide; unassimilated material may also be egested.
It obtains its starting organic carbon from other organisms rather than fixing inorganic carbon as its principal carbon source.

title: Respiration in producers and consumers

steps.text: Autotrophs also respire, oxidizing carbon compounds to supply ATP.
In darkness, photosynthetic carbon dioxide uptake is absent or negligible while respiration continues.
Chemical energy is transferred into ATP and ultimately dissipated as heat; accept chemical energy to heat during respiration.
The dispersed low-grade heat is not available to drive the same biological work; continued external energy input is required.

stem: A sealed transparent microcosm contains plants, decomposers, mineral nutrients, water and air. It receives light and transfers heat to its surroundings, but no matter is deliberately added or removed.

steps.text: Closed to matter but open to energy; it is a closed system, not an isolated one.
They break down organic matter and release mineral nutrients into forms that can be reused by producers.
Organisms also require other elements, such as nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur, which must be available and recycled.
Energy is dissipated as heat during metabolism and cannot be recycled into an equivalent usable biological supply; light replenishes the input.
Gas balance, nutrient availability, species interactions or physical conditions may become unsuitable even if matter is retained; award one developed reason.
